label: January 1917
headline: Peace Without Victory
deck: President Wilson speaks for a peace between equals as the U-boats wait
caption: A U-boat lies surfaced beside a sinking steamer in a winter swell
body: On 22 January President Wilson tells the American Senate that the war should end in a 'peace without victory'. Only a peace between equals, imposed on neither side, can last, he says, and he proposes a league of nations to keep it.

On 19 January fire at a munitions works at Silvertown, in London's East End, sets off some fifty tons of TNT. The explosion kills seventy-three people, flattens whole streets and is heard across the city.
In Sinai, mounted troops of the Desert Column take the Turkish post at Rafa on 9 January, on the border of Palestine, after a day of fighting; the railway follows them across the desert.
On the last day of the month the German ambassador hands Washington a note: from 1 February, U-boats will sink without warning in the waters around Britain, France and Italy.
briefs: The liner Laurentic, carrying gold, sinks on mines off Ireland
The Danish West Indies pass to the United States by treaty
British troops attack along the Tigris below Kut
